independentDerivation: a and b are positive reciprocals. Under u=1/x, dx=-du/u^2, x=a maps to u=b and x=b maps to u=a. Substitution gives -u^2/((1+u)(1+u^6)) du; reversing limits gives I=integral_a^b u^2/((1+u)(1+u^6)) du. Adding to the original gives 2I=integral_a^b (x^3+x^2)/((1+x)(1+x^6)) dx=integral_a^b x^2/(1+x^6) dx. A primitive is (1/3) arctan(x^3). Since b^3=sqrt(3) and a^3=1/sqrt(3), 2I=(1/3)(pi/3-pi/6)=pi/18 and I=pi/36. The worked solution and short answer are correct.
